fact: Qrest has finite Lebesgue volume, and the product of the two restricted box measures in S002 is finite.
justification: Apply Measure.pi.isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts now with Fin k and real components, using BG016 and BG017. Qrest is compact by BG020, so it has finite measure. The real interval has finite measure by BG016 and BG019. Their product has finite total measure (the product of the two finite masses); equivalently, BG003–BG004 and the measure-preserving bijection identify its total mass with volume(Q)<∞ from N002. Boundedness of d∘I on the box also follows directly from the N002 bound on d on Q. Integrability needed by M012 was independently checked through BG006 and BG008, exactly the alternative justification in S002.

grounds.reason: Provides finite volume of Q and boundedness on Q of the d section.
d is the ∂_{x_j}(ut·dxu) section and is integrable.
Defines Qrest and the restricted product measure and proves the insertion box correspondence.

fact: For each fixed z∈Qrest, the function y↦d(I(y,z)) is continuous on ℝ.
justification: Use Continuous.comp with continuous d from F001 and the coordinate-line insertion y↦I(y,z). The latter's jth coordinate is y and all its other coordinates are fixed components of z, so it is a continuous affine map in the finite-coordinate topology. All y are allowed because time is fixed at t0>0. This verifies continuity for the second M003 application.

grounds.reason: d is smooth, and N002 additionally gives its continuity.
I is explicitly coordinate insertion.
z is fixed in Qrest before forming the real-line slice.

fact: Once each inner set integral in F002 is zero, its outer integral over Qrest is zero.
justification: For every z∈Qrest, M007 and the zero endpoint values give the inner integral zero, with the oriented/set-integral conversion checked by BG011–BG012. Substitute the identically-zero integrand on the domain of the outer restricted measure and use MeasureTheory.integral_zero with real codomain. Thus F002 indeed yields ∫_Q d=0. No integrability claim for arbitrary unbounded functions or limit interchange is used.

grounds.reason: F002 supplies the exact iterated-integral representation.
The inner set integral is proved zero for every z in Qrest before the outer integral is evaluated.

fact: Smooth maps on the positive-time domain have smooth fixed-positive-time spatial sections and smooth coordinate-line sections.
justification: Apply ContDiffOn.comp with outer set ℝ^n×(0,∞), inner set the whole spatial space or real line, and affine maps x↦(x,t0) or y↦(x with coordinate j replaced by y,t0). Every component of these affine maps is a constant or a coordinate projection, so they are smooth. The MapsTo premise holds everywhere because t0>0. Smoothness on the whole inner domain is precisely smoothness of the section; no time extension or derivative interchange is used. ContDiff.comp (also probed as M115) handles ordinary globally defined spatial compositions, but M131 checks the open-time-domain version here.

grounds.reason: u is jointly smooth on the positive-time domain.
ut and dxu are smooth on that domain.
t0>0 is fixed and all coordinate-line variations are spatial.
